title: Two hundred thousand API calls
arc: Meridian needs weather for every trip to price surge fairly, and the weather partner allows ten calls a second. A loop would take a week; a thousand threads would get you blocked. This week you learn when work is waiting and when it is computing: threads, the GIL, processes, asyncio, rate limits and backpressure, and measuring before optimising. By Friday the enrichment runs within the partner's limit and you can say why each tool fits.
previously: Is calling an API waiting or computing? Why does that decide the tool?
Why didn't threads speed up the CPU-heavy part?
Recall: what does a token bucket allow, and what does it smooth out?
What should you measure before you optimise anything?
cliff: Ten calls a second, two hundred thousand trips. How long, and how do you shorten it?
The GIL is real. When does it not matter at all?
The partner blocked your key. What should have stopped you?
Next: Meridian's trips table has three different "trip counts". Which one is right?

scenes.monday: Tomas wants weather on every trip by next week. The partner allows ten calls a second. A plain loop would take days. Start with waiting versus computing.
scenes.midweek: Someone ran the enrichment with a hundred threads and the partner blocked Meridian's key for an hour. Build a token bucket and limit concurrent calls so it never happens again.
scenes.friday: The job is still slower than it should be. Measure before you change anything: find the slow part, then decide between threads, processes and asyncio with numbers.
